html:
The Tojolabal, who call themselves Tojolwinik'otik ("true people"), are a Maya people of the highlands and plains around Comitán and Las Margaritas in Chiapas, southern Mexico, near the Guatemalan border. Their language is closest to Chuj, spoken just across the border.

For centuries many Tojolabal worked as labourers on large estates owned by landowners of Comitán. Land reform in the 1900s let many communities win their own common land. Tojolabal villages were among the bases of the Zapatista uprising of 1 January 1994, when rebels took Las Margaritas and other Chiapas towns. Their neighbours include the Lacandon to the east.
